text:
**Short answer:** for most campers, a 250-500Wh unit is the right size. The one I'd pick is the **Anker SOLIX C300** or **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus**. If you need to run a fridge or stay out several days, step up to the **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 or 2000 v2**.

## Weekend tent or car camping (about 270-290Wh)
These cover phones, lights, a camera and a CPAP for a few nights, and weigh 8-10 lb.

| Model | Approx. price | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Anker SOLIX C300 | ~$199 | Built-in lantern, 5-year warranty. Make sure you get the AC-outlet version, not the "C300 DC". |
| Jackery Explorer 300 Plus | ~$249 | Lightest at 8.3 lb, simple to use. Jackery has replaced it with the 300 v2, so check current stock. |
| EcoFlow River 3 Plus | ~$269-299 | 600W inverter, expandable to 572Wh. |
| Bluetti EB3A | ~$179 | Cheapest real LiFePO4 option, 600W inverter. |

Source: [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/). That site earns affiliate commissions, and its prices are approximate.

The lab-tested [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station) scored the Jackery 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) fairly low against bigger units. That's partly because small units naturally score lower on power and runtime. They're still fine if your needs are modest. Don't treat them as clear winners.

## Multi-day trips, electric cooler, or van/overland use
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** was OutdoorGearLab's best for off-grid camping. It scored 81, delivers 2,200W, weighs 39 lb, and was listed under $900 on Amazon. It has no battery expansion. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (~$799) is TechRadar's pick for camping. ([TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations))
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** is WIRED's pick for camping at about $1,079-$1,199. It is IP65-rated, weighs just under 40 lb, and has a 5-year warranty. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/))

## Best mid-size value
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** was OutdoorGearLab's best value, listed under $530. It's compact at 25 lb but has a noisy fan. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Bluetti AC180** (1,152Wh, 1,800W, 5-year warranty) is $499, or **$474.05 with code AFF5OFF**. The code was tested in Bluetti's cart on 2026-10-21. [Buy at Bluetti via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). This is an affiliate link, and checkout has the final word on price.

I couldn't pull direct retailer links for the other models. The review pages above have the buy buttons, so check the price there before ordering. Black Friday is coming, so prices on these may drop soon.

**Tip:** turn off a CPAP's heated humidifier, since it can triple the power draw.

If you tell me what you'll run (fridge, CPAP, laptop), how many nights, and your budget, I can narrow this to one pick.
